english.title: Disclose protected information disclosed by a public authority acting as an anti-fraud organisation
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) disclosed protected information knowing, suspecting, or having reasonable grounds for suspecting, that it was information of a kind that had been disclosed by a public authority, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PUBLIC AUTHORITY..),

(A)_[as a result of that public authority being a member of]_
(B)_[otherwise than in accordance with arrangements made by]_

a specified anti-fraud organisation, that information

(C)_[having been so disclosed by the public authority to you]_
(D)_[having come into your possession as a result of such a disclosure by the public authority to another person]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 69(1) and 70(1) of the Serious Crime Act 2007.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
disclosed protected information knowing/suspecting/having reasonable grounds for suspecting
that it was information of a kind that had been disclosed by a public authority
as a result of that public authority being a member of a specified anti-fraud organisation or
otherwise than in accordance with arrangements made by such an organisation
that information having been so disclosed by the public authority to you OR
that information having come into your possession
as a result of such a disclosure by the public authority to another person

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 69(2) and (3) for circumstances where section 69(1) does not apply to disclosures made.
(ii) See section 69(4) for a defence to a section 69(1) offence.
(iii) See sections 69(5), (6) and (7) for explanation of various terms used in this offence.
(iv) See section 70(2) for the consent by Director of Public Prosecutions required for a prosecution.
(v) See section 70(4) for the liability of officers of a body corporate.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Note:
The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022, see paragraph 8 of Schedule 13 to this Act; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 70(1) and (5A) of the Serious Crime Act 2007 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
